Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Preserve scope and constraints. Do not invent context, requirements, or missing information. Do not perform the task.", "input": "
could you turn this into a practical repair-plan prompt for the person who will prepare a paper for Meadowbank Community Library? it needs to be something trustees and volunteers can use, not a report saying work is finished. Please address it to Leonie, not Ellis. Keep the meeting notes in the prompt so the writer has the actual source material, and ask for a plan that separates confirmed details from estimates and things nobody has checked yet. We need a usable order of work, likely responsibilities, timing, access and safety points, and a clear account of the money, but don't have the writer pretend that an estimate is an approved quote or fill in missing answers.

These are notes from the library repair meeting on Wednesday 13 August 2025. Meadowbank is in a converted shop and all public rooms are on one floor. It is normally open Tuesday and Thursday from 10 to 6, and Saturday from 9 to 1. The entrance threshold has a split in the timber near the right-hand door. No one has measured how deep it is; a volunteer put a yellow marker beside it after a visitor caught a shoe there last week. Nobody was hurt, but Jon said the marker must stay until a repair or other safe arrangement is agreed. The entrance is the only step-free public entrance, so the plan cannot just send wheelchair users round the back.

The north reading room ceiling has a brown stain that appeared after heavy rain on 6 August. Asha saw one small drip that evening, but no one has seen water coming through since. The ceiling has not been opened, and the source of the leak is unknown. There is no report of damage to the electrical fittings; do not turn that into a professional inspection or a guarantee that the wiring is safe. The reading room is still in use, though the treasurer suggested moving the two fabric chairs while the area is checked. A local roofing firm has given Jon an estimate of £1,450 to inspect the roof and patch the likely entry point. It is an estimate, not an accepted quotation, and it excludes internal ceiling repairs. No visit date has been offered.

There are two loose shelving bays along the east wall. They wobble when the top shelf is loaded, but nobody has found a broken upright. Ewan tightened one visible screw by hand and stopped because he did not know whether the fixings behind the shelf were suitable. He has not tested the bays since. The meeting thought a pair of volunteers might be able to help, but that was not an approval for them to dismantle or load the units. Include a safe way to decide who should assess them and when books can be moved back. The children’s story group uses the nearby rug on Saturdays at 10, so noise, loose books and a work area need to be handled around that session.

At the outside ramp, paint is flaking from the handrail. There is no report that the rail moves, and nobody has checked underneath the paint for corrosion. A decorating contractor estimated £210 to scrape and repaint it, with the work taking one day in dry weather. The contractor warned that rain would delay the job. The ramp is part of the accessible route, so keep a usable route in the plan while any work is happening. Marisol, the council property officer, said by phone that a sketch must be submitted at least 10 business days before exterior work on the ramp. She has not confirmed whether this particular repaint needs a permit. No written approval has arrived.

Jon also got a quote for the entrance threshold from a joiner: £680 including materials, with two days’ notice needed to book. The quote does not say how long the repair itself will take or whether the entrance needs to close during it. Do not guess those details. All three prices—the roof estimate, ramp estimate and joiner quote—are the only figures in the notes. The £2,400 in the library’s unrestricted repairs fund is available for repairs, according to Asha. There is a separate £600 memorial gift, but the meeting agreed it is not to be used for building work. The insurance policy has a £500 excess for water damage; no claim has been made and no one knows whether the roof issue would be covered. Show the possible relevance of the excess without treating coverage as confirmed.

The council owns the building. The library cannot close for more than one day, and trustees have not chosen a closure date. Keep normal opening times in view and flag where contractor dates or noise could conflict with public use. The board review is scheduled for Tuesday 26 August. Asha wants cost figures shown as estimates or quotes as appropriate, with unknown internal ceiling costs left visibly unknown. Jon asked that the plan distinguish work that might be done by a competent volunteer from work needing a contractor, but nobody at the meeting decided who counts as competent for any task. Do not assign named people a job they have not accepted.

Please ask the plan writer to arrange the source notes in a practical sequence, while retaining each distinct issue and its status. A numbered work table would be useful if it can show issue, evidence or uncertainty, proposed next step, responsibility to be confirmed, access or safety consideration, timing dependency and cost source. Include a short section on decisions trustees need to make at the 26 August review, without deciding for them. The plan should be suitable for circulation to trustees and volunteers, state that it is based on these meeting notes, and avoid presenting any work, permission, booking, inspection or insurance decision as already completed.

One more point from the notes: Maya, who chaired the meeting, said, “Let’s keep the doorway open in the plan, even if the repair date has to wait.” Record that as a concern about access, not as confirmation that the joiner can work without closing the entrance. There was no agreed start date, no confirmed contractor booking and no response yet from the council about the roof. Please keep those gaps visible rather than supplying an answer for them.", "output": "Prepare a practical repair plan for Meadowbank Community Library for circulation to its trustees and volunteers. Address it to Leonie, not Ellis. The plan should help readers decide what to do next; it must not suggest that any repair, inspection, booking, permission or insurance decision has already been completed. Base it on the meeting notes below, retaining the status of each fact, estimate, quote, uncertainty and outstanding decision. Do not invent missing answers or treat estimates as approved quotations.

Organize the plan in a useful sequence. Include a numbered work table, if suitable, with columns for the issue, evidence or uncertainty, proposed next step, responsibility to be confirmed, access or safety consideration, timing dependency and cost source. Distinguish possible competent-volunteer work from work that needs a contractor, but do not decide who is competent or assign work to anyone who has not accepted it. Include the decisions trustees need to make at their review on Tuesday 26 August, without making those decisions for them. Keep unknown costs visibly unknown.

### Source meeting notes — Wednesday 13 August 2025

Meadowbank Community Library occupies a converted shop, with all public rooms on one floor. Normal opening hours are Tuesday and Thursday, 10 to 6, and Saturday, 9 to 1. The library cannot close for more than one day, and trustees have not chosen a closure date. Keep public use and normal opening times in view when considering contractor dates, noise and work areas.

1. **Entrance threshold and accessible access.** The timber threshold near the right-hand door is split. Its depth has not been measured. After a visitor caught a shoe there last week, a volunteer placed a yellow marker beside it. Nobody was hurt. Jon said the marker must remain until a repair or another safe arrangement is agreed. This is the only step-free public entrance; wheelchair users cannot simply be sent round the back. Jon obtained a joiner’s quote of £680, including materials, with two days’ notice needed to book. The quote does not say how long the repair will take or whether the entrance would need to close. Do not guess either detail. Maya, who chaired the meeting, said, “Let’s keep the doorway open in the plan, even if the repair date has to wait.” Treat this as an access concern, not confirmation that the joiner can work without closing the entrance.

2. **North reading room ceiling and roof.** A brown stain appeared after heavy rain on 6 August. Asha saw one small drip that evening, but nobody has seen water coming through since. The ceiling has not been opened, and the leak’s source is unknown. There is no report of damage to the electrical fittings. Do not present that as a professional inspection or a guarantee that the wiring is safe. The room remains in use. Asha suggested moving the two fabric chairs while the area is checked. A local roofing firm gave Jon an estimate of £1,450 to inspect the roof and patch the likely entry point. This is an estimate, not an accepted quotation; it excludes internal ceiling repairs, and no visit date has been offered. The council has not responded about the roof.

3. **East-wall shelving.** Two shelving bays wobble when the top shelf is loaded. Nobody has found a broken upright. Ewan tightened one visible screw by hand, then stopped because he did not know whether the fixings behind the shelf were suitable. He has not tested the bays since. The meeting thought two volunteers might be able to help, but did not approve them to dismantle or load the units. Set out how someone should assess the bays and when books could be moved back, without assuming the assessment or work has happened. The children’s story group uses the nearby rug on Saturdays at 10. Account for noise, loose books and the work area around that session.

4. **Ramp handrail.** Paint is flaking from the outside ramp’s handrail. Nobody has reported that the rail moves, and nobody has checked for corrosion beneath the paint. A decorating contractor estimated £210 to scrape and repaint it, with one day of work in dry weather; rain would delay the job. The ramp is part of the accessible route, so maintain a usable route during any work. Marisol, the council property officer, said by phone that a sketch must be submitted at least 10 business days before exterior work on the ramp. She has not confirmed whether this repaint needs a permit, and no written approval has arrived.

### Costs, authority and open decisions

The three figures in the notes are the £1,450 roof estimate, the £210 ramp estimate and the £680 joiner quote. Asha said the unrestricted repairs fund has £2,400 available for repairs. There is also a separate £600 memorial gift, which the meeting agreed must not be used for building work. The insurance policy has a £500 excess for water damage. No claim has been made, and nobody knows whether the roof issue would be covered. Explain the possible relevance of the excess without treating coverage as confirmed. The council owns the building. Jon wants the plan to distinguish work that might be suitable for a competent volunteer from work needing a contractor; the meeting did not decide who is competent for any task. Do not name anyone as responsible for work they have not accepted.

Make clear that there is no agreed start date, no confirmed contractor booking and no response yet from the council about the roof. Identify timing or access questions that remain unresolved, and leave the unknown internal ceiling cost unknown. Present the plan as a tool for the 26 August board review, not as a record of decisions already made."}]
